checks.label: On 230 V the supply peaks at 230 × √2 = 325 V. The half-wave averages 207 V over its hump, and 325 ÷ π = 104 V over the whole cycle, 0.318 of the peak
The full-wave average is 2 × 0.318 = 0.637 of the peak voltage, assuming no diode losses: the bridge averages 207 V on 230 V, twice the half-wave
Regardless of the polarity of the input, the current flows in the same direction through the load: D1 and D2 carry the positive half, D3 and D4 the negative, and the output never goes below zero
The ripple frequency is twice the supply frequency: the bridge output has two humps a cycle, 100 a second on a 50 Hz supply
The probe on D1 reads 0 while D1 conducts, and peaks at 270°: 325 V in a 230 V bridge, and 115 × √2 = 163 V in a 115 V one
Six-pulse on 400 V: the output dips to cos 30° × 566 = 490 V and averages 3√2 ÷ π × 400 = 540 V; on 440 V it averages 594 V under 622 V tops
In the six-pulse the output is the largest line-to-line voltage, the conducting pair changes six times a cycle (every 60°), and the probe on L1's upper diode peaks at the 566 V line-to-line peak
With D3 open the bridge works as a half-wave: nothing in the negative half, and a 104 V average
Silicon diodes have a forward voltage of approximately 0.7 volts: two in the current's path take 1.4 V, about 12% of a 12 V output and under 1% of 207 V
The drawing makes the conducting diodes bold and draws the arrow through the load, pointing down, only while current flows
Each puzzle offers three answers and accepts only its right one, every wrong answer has its own hint, and nothing in the picture shows the answer before Check
Each demonstration sweep ends within 4.5 s of its screen opening, and a right answer shows within 3 s of Check
